sites.functional_impact_measured: Folding and trafficking explicitly stated non-perturbative (PMC13382790); surface display confirmed by anti-myc flow cytometry on non-permeabilized cells and by immunofluorescence (PMC9860121, PMC13382790); stable expression in RSCs with dose-dependent plasma-membrane trafficking quantified (PMC13382790); HA-tagged mouse PMP22 in ECL2 confirmed unaffected processing and trafficking (PMC3563111); myc-tagged human PMP22 in ECL2 confirmed no interference with cellular transport or function (PMC9860121).
sites.rationale: The ledger entry from PMC13382790 explicitly names residues 125 and 126 as the junction for a 10-residue myc epitope tag in ECL2 of human PMP22. Python computation confirms: residue 125 = H, residue 126 = L, both within ECL2 (topology landmarks 117–133). Distance from TM3 C-boundary (residue 116) to the insert = 9 residues; distance from insert to TM4 N-boundary (residue 134) = 8 residues; both well above the ≥3 residue minimum. The insert sits centrally in a 17-residue extracellular loop, sterically plausible for a 15–23 aa ALFA tag with GS linkers. Multiple independent publications using HA (mouse, PMC3563111) and myc (human, PMC8191293, PMC9860121, PMC3110552, PMC13293285, PMC12881431) tags in the same ECL2 all confirm non-perturbative behaviour, providing strong convergent support. The C-terminal ALFA (DOI:10.1101/2025.09.03.673966) and C-terminal GFP (PMC11700639) tags are on the intracellular face (topology: residues 157–160 = INTRACELLULAR) and are excluded. No ledger entry pins any insertion in ECL1 (26–66) to a specific residue. [validation: surface_and_function; position: inferred; source: paper; entailment_verified: True]

sources.claim: The 10-residue myc tag was inserted between residues 125 and 126 in the second extracellular loop of PMP22, as this internal tag was previously demonstrated to be non-perturbative of PMP22 folding and trafficking ( Fig. 1 A ) ( 36 , 37 ).
